messages:
Anya C: RFC kickoff — we need to converge on a single proposal that ties kernel selection, an attention shortcut optimization, and a KV eviction policy together for Dedicated customers with mixed-latency workloads. customer asks (Acme) are pushing this into Q2 prioritization.

Mike R: +1. can we scope this so the runtime can choose a kernel per-request based on budget + seq_len distro? thinking: fast-path kernels for short responses, high-throughput kernels for long streams.

Carmen L: agree. acceptance criteria we should require:
- no >5% p99 latency regressions on any paid tier during canary
- token-cost improvement >= 8% for target workloads (chat + summarization)
- graceful fallback to current kernel on OOM or perf anomaly

Priya (PM): Acme specifically asked for: predictable 99th percentile under bursty traffic and ability to cap cost per request. they're okay with a short degradation in mean latency if p99 holds. this affects Dedicated pricing asks.

Luke W: operational questions: rollout plan? canary per-customer or per-region? what's the flag matrix?

Anya C: proposal: staged rollout
1) internal perf eval + microbenchmarks (bench fleet)
2) canary on non-Dedicated hosted region with synthetic bursts
3) opt-in Dedicated customers (Acme as partner canary)
4) global opt-out safe flag + automatic fallback if error rate or p99 exceeds thresholds

Mike R: + details on the selector heuristics:
- input signals: seq_len_estimate, kv_cache_hit_ratio, target_latency_budget, model_variant
- decision model: small rule engine + percentile thresholds, fallback to static mapping when uncertain

Carmen L: edge cases to call out in RFC:
- extremely long prompting (100k tokens) -> kernel must avoid OOM via streaming recompute or chunked-attn
- mixed-precision/model quantization differences -> perf varies, need per-model profiles
- KV cold-starts cause spikes; eviction policy should prefer LRU with weighted recency by request importance

Priya (PM): business gating items:
- SLA doc updated to include kernel fallback behavior
- pricing note for Dedicated customers if cost reduces (credits or pass-through?)
- legal signoff on telemetry collection for per-request routing

Luke W: experiment metrics (proposal):
- primary: p99 latency, p50, median tokens/sec, cost-per-token delta
- secondary: model output similarity (ROUGE/BERTScore on eval prompts) to detect quality regressions
- safety: error rate, OOM rate, fallback frequency

Anya C: short config sketch for runtime selector (for RFC):
```json
{
  "selector": {
    "rules": [
      {"if": "seq_len < 64 && kv_hit_ratio > 0.8", "kernel": "fast-lowmem"},
      {"if": "seq_len >= 64 && seq_len < 1024", "kernel": "balanced"},
      {"if": "seq_len >= 1024", "kernel": "streaming-recompute"}
    ],
    "fallback": "balanced",
    "telemetry": {"emit_route_decision": true}
  },
  "kv_eviction": {"policy": "weighted_lru", "weights": {"recency": 0.7, "importance": 0.3}}
}
```

Mike R: testing notes: please add microbench harness for mixed-precision (fp16/4-bit) and a cold-kv benchmark. also include a stress runner that simulates 40% tail traffic spikes.

Carmen L: acceptance test checklist for PRD/RFC docs:
- bench report attached with baseline vs candidate across representative models (chat, summarization, codegen)
- rollout playbook with rollback triggers and runbooks for OOM/fallback floods
- per-route telemetry dashboard mockups (p99 by kernel, fallback rate, kv hit heatmap)

Priya (PM): timeline ask: can we aim for RFC ready for eng-prioritization review next Wed? Acme demo window is 6 weeks out so we need clear canary milestones.

Anya C: I'll draft RFC tonight and include: motivation, design, configs, acceptance criteria, rollout plan, experiment plan, and a short customer impact note. tagging @Mike R @Carmen L for review. :eyes:

deploy-bot: RFC created — link: https://r.infra/rfc/7423 (internal).

Luke W: thanks. next steps: Anya to post draft, Mike/Carmen to add perf test cases, Priya to finalize customer success plan.

Priya (PM): will sync legal and pricing today and drop notes in the RFC thread.

Carmen L: quick call? 30m to align on edge-case tests tomorrow 10am PT?

Anya C: yes — booked.

Mike R: adding a checklist item: run comparative compilation with the new kernel selection to see JIT/compile overheads on cold start.

Anya C: noted. action items appended to RFC. :thumbsup:
